ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Protein $Arkkkk60491$ mediates the enzymatic catalysis of the reaction necessary to produce dog saliva. $Arkkkk60491$ is a homodimer, and each subunit is composed of $337$ amino acids. Figure $1$ represents the modular structure of this homodimer, in which three positions are marked: position $A$ is the active site, position $B$ contains a large number of nonpolar residues, and position $C$ contains a large number of charged residues. A mutation has now been found that changes a positively charged lysine residue into a negatively charged glutamic acid residue, and this single change directly affects the position where the substrate attaches during the catalytic process. Which position is this change most likely to affect?
